$comment: WS-C.1b boundary guard — temporary allowlist of files still holding vapour-pressure/ET0 formulas outside the Weather Engine. Enforced by scripts/ci/weather_engine_formula_guard.py. New occurrences NOT on this list fail CI. Entries are TEMPORARY: removed as consumers migrate to the Weather Engine ET0 product (C.1b delegation + C.2 BFF); once a consumer is migrated, delete its formula and its allowlist entry — the file then failing CI is the intended ratchet.

temporary_legacy_allowlist.note: Platform's ET0 core (penman_monteith_et0/hargreaves_et0/_svp) — still the operational ET0 for the irrigation recommendation path. Retire after platform delegates to the Weather Engine ET0 product (shadow-compare first, then remove). NOT shadow-only yet.
Platform ET0 Penman-Monteith over WeatherInput — consumed by the irrigation recommendation. Migrate to the Weather Engine ET0 product, then remove.
Platform FAO-56 helpers (penman_monteith_et0 delegating to core.engines.et0; also holds gdd_daily/gdd_accumulate). Retire alongside the et0.py core migration.

Platform GDD daily kernel variant (gdd_day, Baskerville-Emin modified method) inside the RUE season sim. Migrate the daily kernel to the Weather Engine gdd.py (method='modified'); _CROP_PARAMS stays as Season policy. NOTE: this is a GDD (C.1c) entry, NOT ET0 — season ET0 is already fully delegated to the engine ET0 series.

WS-C.1b audit found an INLINE Hargreaves-Samani ET0 re-implementation (Ra + 0.0023*(Tmean+17.8)*sqrt(dT)*Ra*0.408) in the MCP weather tool server — a genuine second ET0 kernel outside the engine that previously ESCAPED this guard (neither the SVP fingerprint nor a name-matched function). Now caught via the Hargreaves math fingerprint. Migrate the MCP tool to call the Weather Engine ET0 product, then delete the inline formula and this entry.

`_hargreaves_et0` is a thin wrapper delegating to core.engines.et0.hargreaves_et0 (no inline math). Caught now via the broadened `hargreaves`-substring name match so the ET0 path is monitored, not invisible. Migrate the weather-analytics endpoint to the Weather Engine ET0 product, then remove the wrapper + this entry.

`_et0_from_weather_payload` produces a LOCAL ET0 by calling api.water_balance.compute_et0 (which delegates to core.engines.et0) and drives the field-state ETc block. No inline formula, but a live local-ET0 producer — caught now via the `_et0_from` name so it is tracked. Migrate to the Weather Engine ET0 product, then remove this entry.
